meta_description_en: Editorial for Outlet issue #009: DISCiPLE and Plus D support, updated subscription rates, freeware policy, and an overview of the issue contents.
meta_description_ru: Редакционная колонка Outlet #009: поддержка систем DISCiPLE и Plus D, новые тарифы на подписку, политика в отношении freeware и обзор софта выпуска.
body_en_plain:
Well,this is the first new issue
of OUTLET with Disciple and Plus
D versions(back issues available
of course) so WELCOME! Still may
be one or  two problems to solve
(tell us!)but generally it looks
very good - Should be new faces,
new ideas and new programs!

There's YET ANOTHER control in
ROTATOR (Issue 7)! Key "9" moves
the grid "away";key "0" moves it
"nearer".If you want the prompts
and instructions changed, MERGE
in "ROTMOD" from this issue.

And now for the BAD news .....
We are sorry to  say  that  some
adjustments have had to be  made
to the selling prices of OUTLET.

The GOOD news is .... the basic
price of an issue remains the
same, only subscriptions have
been increased slightly. The
reason being that, at the start
of OUTLET, we offered huge
discounts on subscriptions
before we knew, with accuracy,
what the running costs of the


magazine would be. With eight
months behind us, it is now
apparent that we must be a
little more conservative with
the discount percentages if
OUTLET is to remain viable.

The next GOOD news is.....
the OLD subscription prices will
remain valid to established
readers of OUTLET until 1st
September 1988! Thanks for your
support!(Cripes, what a bargain!
Where's my cheque book!)

The new order forms will be
going out over the next month
or two so hang onto one of the
old forms if you want to take
out a subscription between now
and the deadline.

Here's the full tariff:

No. of    On our       On your
months    disc/cart    disc/cart
------    ---------    ---------
twin cart:-
 1          ` 5.00       ` 2.00
 6          `29.00       `11.00
12          `57.00       `21.00


single cart:-
 1          ` 3.00       ` 1.00
 6          `14.75       ` 5.75
12          `29.00       `11.00


disc:-
 1          ` 3.50       ` 2.00
 6          `18.50       `11.00
12          `35.00       `21.00

We may,from time to time,include
"FREEWARE" in OUTLET - that is
"Public Domain" software.This is
software that you can FREELY
copy and give away to others but
it should show the author's name
prominently and a statement that
it can be copied to others. It
should not be sold for profit
but a modest charge may be made
to cover costs. We've given some
thought to where we stand in all
this because OUTLET's a commerc-
ial enterprise but we now think
that any FREEWARE programs pub-
lished in OUTLET be regarded as
given FREE with the magazine.

Having said all that, TRI-LOADER
in Issue 8 may be treated as
public domain and,in this issue,

on the B cartridge, TIME TO GO
ERM. We've also just produced a
sampler demo of OUTLET which has
JOTTER, JIG!BLOX, some title
screens from various programs,
and a selection of text items so
that possible new readers will
be able to get an idea of what
OUTLET is like before buying.The
whole of the demo is FREEWARE.

Right! Let's whiz through this
month's contents: ZAP erases
selected blocks of files on Opus
disc or microdrive; RANDOM WALK
is a pattern generator; TEE EM
converts Tasword 2 files to mbx
pages in the VTX500 ENHANCE
format; LIFE is a version of
Conway's classic; SHOUTBURST
replies to Issue 7's item on
violence; CHECKOUT 1 reviews an

interesting new package of Opus
disc utilities. Also on disc and
Cartridge B are CHECKOUT 2 which
looks at an inexpensive video
digitizer; HURRYDUMP - a handy,
text-only COPY to your printer;
SPRINGLES explores hypercycloid
patterns; there's the final
episode of "THAT'S THE TICKET!";
CHANGE - a currency convertor;
SKIPPER - a brilliant utility to
speed up the BASIC editor cursor
and then there's erm... TIME TO
GO "ERM?..."which is erm, a nice
little timepiece!

Many readers wanted to be able
to print out the CONTENTS page.
We looked at different ways but
the one which uses least memory
is just to re-print it here so
you can use the usual routines:-

    OUTLET Issue 9 CONTENTS

      A               B

  Editorial      Checkout 2
  Outletters 1   Hurrydump
  Outletters 2   Springles
  Zap            That Ticket!
  Outboard       Change
  Random Walk    Skipper
  Lookout!       Time to go Erm
  Tee-em
  Life
  Shoutburst
  Checkout 1
  Look Ahead
  ROTMOD

Note that "ROTMOD" is not linked
and cannot be loaded in from the
CONTENTS page


Finally, we received NO entrants
for our "Guess the games" compe-
tition in Issue 7. Fair enough.
It seemed like a good idea at
the time! We won't repeat that
type of competition though.

Have a nice mag!


      Ron & Brian Cavers

  Birstall,Leicester LE4 4NJ
  Prestel Mailbox: 014703943.

body_en:
## Editorial

Well, this is the first new issue of OUTLET with Disciple and Plus D versions (back issues available of course) so WELCOME! Still may be one or two problems to solve (tell us!) but generally it looks very good — Should be new faces, new ideas and new programs!

There's YET ANOTHER control in ROTATOR (Issue 7)! Key "9" moves the grid "away"; key "0" moves it "nearer". If you want the prompts and instructions changed, MERGE in "ROTMOD" from this issue.

And now for the BAD news ..... We are sorry to say that some adjustments have had to be made to the selling prices of OUTLET.

The GOOD news is .... the basic price of an issue remains the same, only subscriptions have been increased slightly. The reason being that, at the start of OUTLET, we offered huge discounts on subscriptions before we knew, with accuracy, what the running costs of the magazine would be. With eight months behind us, it is now apparent that we must be a little more conservative with the discount percentages if OUTLET is to remain viable.

The next GOOD news is..... the OLD subscription prices will remain valid to established readers of OUTLET until 1st September 1988! Thanks for your support! (Cripes, what a bargain! Where's my cheque book!)

The new order forms will be going out over the next month or two so hang onto one of the old forms if you want to take out a subscription between now and the deadline.

Here's the full tariff:

| No. of months | On our disc/cart | On your disc/cart |
|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| **twin cart:-** | | |
| 1 | £ 5.00 | £ 2.00 |
| 6 | £29.00 | £11.00 |
| 12 | £57.00 | £21.00 |
| **single cart:-** | | |
| 1 | £ 3.00 | £ 1.00 |
| 6 | £14.75 | £ 5.75 |
| 12 | £29.00 | £11.00 |
| **disc:-** | | |
| 1 | £ 3.50 | £ 2.00 |
| 6 | £18.50 | £11.00 |
| 12 | £35.00 | £21.00 |

We may, from time to time, include "FREEWARE" in OUTLET — that is "Public Domain" software. This is software that you can FREELY copy and give away to others but it should show the author's name prominently and a statement that it can be copied to others. It should not be sold for profit but a modest charge may be made to cover costs. We've given some thought to where we stand in all this because OUTLET's a commercial enterprise but we now think that any FREEWARE programs published in OUTLET be regarded as given FREE with the magazine.

Having said all that, TRI-LOADER in Issue 8 may be treated as public domain and, in this issue, on the B cartridge, TIME TO GO ERM. We've also just produced a sampler demo of OUTLET which has JOTTER, JIG!BLOX, some title screens from various programs, and a selection of text items so that possible new readers will be able to get an idea of what OUTLET is like before buying. The whole of the demo is FREEWARE.

Right! Let's whiz through this month's contents: ZAP erases selected blocks of files on Opus disc or microdrive; RANDOM WALK is a pattern generator; TEE EM converts Tasword 2 files to mbx pages in the VTX500 ENHANCE format; LIFE is a version of Conway's classic; SHOUTBURST replies to Issue 7's item on violence; CHECKOUT 1 reviews an interesting new package of Opus disc utilities. Also on disc and Cartridge B are CHECKOUT 2 which looks at an inexpensive video digitizer; HURRYDUMP — a handy, text-only COPY to your printer; SPRINGLES explores hypercycloid patterns; there's the final episode of "THAT'S THE TICKET!"; CHANGE — a currency convertor; SKIPPER — a brilliant utility to speed up the BASIC editor cursor and then there's erm... TIME TO GO "ERM?..." which is erm, a nice little timepiece!

Many readers wanted to be able to print out the CONTENTS page. We looked at different ways but the one which uses least memory is just to re-print it here so you can use the usual routines:-

```text
    OUTLET Issue 9 CONTENTS

      A               B

  Editorial      Checkout 2
  Outletters 1   Hurrydump
  Outletters 2   Springles
  Zap            That Ticket!
  Outboard       Change
  Random Walk    Skipper
  Lookout!       Time to go Erm
  Tee-em
  Life
  Shoutburst
  Checkout 1
  Look Ahead
  ROTMOD
```

Note that "ROTMOD" is not linked and cannot be loaded in from the CONTENTS page.

Finally, we received NO entrants for our "Guess the games" competition in Issue 7. Fair enough. It seemed like a good idea at the time! We won't repeat that type of competition though.

Have a nice mag!

Ron & Brian Cavers
